meta.name: Ballot Scalp
meta.intro: Every race on the ballot here, every candidate who filed, and the paperwork that proves they are really running. No endorsements, no ratings, no opinions. Just the public record, with a link back to the office that keeps it.

calendar.body: Closed for partisan races. Open to everyone for school board, judges and city seats.

calendar.label: General election
calendar.body: Every registered voter, every remaining race, regardless of party registration.

explainer.heading: Closed primaries, in plain terms
paras: Florida runs closed partisan primaries. For a partisan race (county commission, the Legislature, Governor, Congress) you can only vote in the primary of the party you are registered with.
Nonpartisan races are different. School board, judges, city commission and soil-and-water seats are open to every registered voter in August, whatever your registration says.

One quirk worth knowing: when a write-in candidate qualifies for a partisan seat, the primary closes to that party even if every other candidate is from the same one. Two races on this site work that way.

meta.datesIntro: Two elections decide the seats on this site. Some races finish in August; some finish in November; a few are already settled because nobody filed against the incumbent.
meta.ballotIntro: Tell us where you vote and we will show only the races that can appear on your ballot. Districts are the ones printed on your voter information card.
meta.lookupNote: Not sure which districts you are in? Your Supervisor of Elections will tell you from your address.
meta.colorNote: This site uses no party colors. Red and blue carry meaning in an election, and a neutral index should not borrow it.

disclaimer.heading: This is not an official election site
disclaimer.verifyLabel: Check any of it against the office that keeps it

paras.title: Independent, not governmental
paras.text: Ballot Scalp is an independent project. It is not a government website, and it is not affiliated with, operated by, or endorsed by any Supervisor of Elections, the Florida Division of Elections, any political party, campaign, or candidate.

paras.title: Copied from the public record
paras.text: Every name, date and status is transcribed from those offices' own records: candidate qualifying lists, petition and filing dates, and sample ballots. We add no endorsements, ratings, scores or rankings. No one can pay to appear here, and no one can pay to be left out.

paras.title: The office is the final word
paras.text: Where this site and an elections office disagree, the office is right. Public records change: candidates withdraw, courts redraw districts, and paperwork gets amended after we read it. Treat every entry as a pointer to the source rather than a replacement for it.

meta.financeNote: Figures are cumulative for the 2026 General Election reporting group, read from each county Supervisor of Elections on 2026-08-07. Candidates who file with the Florida Division of Elections report there instead; their rows link to that office.
